# Oxide Launcher 1.7.0

A release whose point is that the gates work. Every one of the problems below was found by a
check that had never actually run, rather than by reading the code.

## The screenshot tests had never run at all

The Paparazzi workflow died in under a second on its NDK step, on every run, since it was
written. It resolved `sdkmanager` into a shell variable and wrote only `ANDROID_HOME` and
`ANDROID_SDK_ROOT` to `$GITHUB_ENV`, but the NDK step is a separate `run` block, so there
`$SDKMANAGER` was empty and the step ran

    ndk;25.2.9519653: line 1: : command not found

So no golden had ever been rendered, and `verify` had nothing to compare against. The goldens
are now in the repository, a dispatch can re-record and commit them, and `verify` fails on
any drift. 75 screens, at 640x360, 1280x760 and 1920x1080.

## The task drawer crashed whenever a task was in it

    IllegalStateException: Vertically scrollable component was measured with an
    infinity maximum height constraints

`OxideDrawerHost` wrapped its content in `verticalScroll`, which gives the child an infinite
maximum height. The task drawer's list is a `LazyColumn`, so it threw during measure. The empty
drawer drew fine, which is exactly why it had been missed. Drawers now take a `scrollable`
flag - the one `OxideSubWindow` already had - and the task drawer passes false. This is the
same constraint that put the launcher on its crash screen in the Home environment card; it
was still latent in the shared drawer host.

## A mod built for another loader could be installed into this one

The dependency install chain ended its compatibility check with

    versionLoaders.isEmpty() || targetLoaders.any { it in versionLoaders }

An empty file-side list does not mean "no loader required". It means the platform tagged the
file with a loader this build has no enum entry for, so the name was dropped on the way in -
and then the file was declared compatible. A NeoForge-only file could be installed into a
Fabric instance, where it can only fail to load. The rule now fails closed, and the whole
matrix is pinned by a test: same loader, a different loader, a multi-loader file, a file
whose tag cannot be read, and a target that states no requirement.

## The launch splash was still the old one

`SplashActivity` is the LAUNCHER activity, and it renders `SplashScreen` whenever components
need unpacking - which is every update, not only the first install. It was the upstream
Material top bar over a `BackgroundCard`, with a `MarqueeText` action button and a
`CircularProgressIndicator` per row. It is now an Oxide surface: an Oxide brand bar drawn from
`OxideLogo`, and the list carries a state badge per item instead of one of four vector
drawables.

## Four more defects the screenshot tests were pointing at

- The FPS chart's reused `Path` was a file-level singleton. `Path()` is a JNI call, so it ran
  during the file's class initialisation, and any JVM unit test that touched one top-level
  function there died with `UnsatisfiedLinkError` - including a test that only wanted to
  divide one `Dp` by another. It is a `ThreadLocal` now, which also stops one draw thread from
  inheriting the previous frame's control points.
- A Discover result card asked the favourites repository whether a project was favourited
  during composition. That launches a load, and the load reads MMKV - so every screenshot that
  rendered a result grid failed at an order-dependent point. The grid now reads the
  repository's loaded flag outside the `remember`, which also subscribes the cards to load
  completion.
- The log source list read `PathManager.DIR_LAUNCHER_LOGS`, a `lateinit` field only
  `OxideApplication.onCreate` assigns, just to decide which row is the folder row. It is a
  parameter now.
- The custom-JRE import row was a greyed-out row while scanning. The project has a test
  asserting these rows do not exist in that form, and the rule is right: a greyed-out
  clickable row reads as "tappable, just not now". The row is hidden while scanning, matching
  the picker above it.

The installed-mods sheet also fell back to a raw numeric project id as a dependency's primary
label when the platform had no title for it. It now says the platform gave no name and drops
the id to the secondary line, where it is still useful for matching two dependencies of the
same project.

## Lint runs again

Lint had not passed once: 244 errors, and CI never reported them because the unit-test step
failed first. 242 were `MissingTranslation`, one per new user-facing string, across 15
locales. The inherited strings are translated by a pipeline outside this repository and the
Oxide strings are new and English-only, so the check could not be satisfied - recording each
string individually had pushed the baseline past 1.8 MB. The check is off, with the reasoning
in the DSL. The other two errors - `LocalContextGetResourceValueCall` in the storage drawer,
where a resource and a resolver were read off `LocalContext` inside a callback - were fixed in
code rather than accepted. Every other finding still sits in the baseline and still fails CI
when it is new.

## Version

This is release v1.7.0. The launcher reports itself as **1.0.0** in About, in the sidebar
footer, on the Home screen and in crash reports. That is deliberate: the release identity and
the product version are different facts. The update check, the HTTP user agent, the JVM
launcher-version argument and the modpack metadata template all keep the build version, because
other software compares against them and they have to move monotonically.

## Verified

Compilation, unit tests, screenshot verification, lint, R8, packaging and signing, through CI.
Not validated on physical hardware - that is what this release is for.
